thread:
Maya L: quick sync — I started a thread to decide how we instrument per-route KPIs in Console for kernel selection + batching + KV behavior. seeing p99 blips on /chat-endpoint and want token-level attributions
Samir: do we have an estimate of tracing overhead? I don't want sampling to tank p50 for small requests :/
Jules: agree. propose 1% full trace (all token events) + capture 100% for requests that hit p95+ so we can repro regressions. that gives us signal without huge cost
Maya L: exactly. also we should capture kernel_id, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, routing_fallback, and model_variant. those are the dims we care about
Ops Bot: profiling-run/1842105123 completed — flamegraph + kernel attribution reports uploaded: https://internal/prof/1842105123 (cc @Maya L) :white_check_mark:
Leo: nice. can we emit a token waterfall metric with breakdown: queueing, kernel_latency, kv_lookup, token_encode, token_decode? that would make p99 root-causing easier
Anya: +1. For KV we need to tag whether item was served from hot-prefix cache vs disk tier. kv_cache_hit alone isn't enough for ops-level triage
Kevin: dashboard ask: layout proposal — top row: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (req/s), error rate. second row: token waterfall sparkline and kernel mix pie. third row: sampling controls + quick links to traces
Samir: for alerting, we should base on adjusted p99 (remove outliers from warmup / redeploy). maybe use rolling window 15m with relative baseline per-route
Jules: implementation note — backend emits per-token events to telemetry with tag kernel_id. here's the Clickhouse proto query I'm testing: ```
SELECT route, kernel_id,
  quantileTDigest(0.5)(token_latency) AS p50,
  quantileTDigest(0.95)(token_latency) AS p95,
  quantileTDigest(0.99)(token_latency) AS p99,
  count() AS tokens
FROM token_events
WHERE ts >= now()-toIntervalHour(1)
GROUP BY route, kernel_id
ORDER BY route, p99 DESC
```
Maya L: looks good. add `kv_cache_tier` as a group by and materialize hourly aggregates for Console to avoid ad-hoc cost
Kevin: UI detail — include an inline toggle: "Show kernel attribution" that overlays kernel p99 on the route curve. also allow drilldown: select kernel -> show sample traces
Samir: a couple of runtime concerns: continuous batching means batch_size correlates with latency; we should include batch_size histogram per route to know if kernel choice was made at wrong batch thresholds
Anya: yes, and include `routing_reason` (e.g., capacity, cost_policy, region_fallback) so we can see if fallbacks are causing regressions
Ops Bot: created issue #IR-672: "Console: per-route token waterfall + kernel attribution + sampling" and assigned to @Jules @Maya L. link: https://tickets/IR-672
Jules: plan for rollout: 1) wire token_events with new fields (kernel_id, kv_cache_tier, batch_size, routing_reason) 2) create hourly aggregates and ddp dashboards 3) enable sampling config in runtime (1% full, 100% p95+) 4) pilot on staging, then gradual prod flip (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
Leo: for pilot, can we keep a cheap fallback that switches kernel to low-cost quantized path if p99 > threshold? we need that as a safety net during rollout
Maya L: safety net: yes, runtime already supports kernel_fallback flag. we'll expose it as a route-level policy in the Console alongside alert thresholds
Kevin: can we add a quick alert rule template: "route p99 > baseline*1.6 AND kernel_fallback_count > 0" — that will catch degradations tied to fallbacks
Samir: one more — instrumentation for GC/OOM: token events should have `mem_pressure` tag so kernel regressions due to memory thrash are visible
Anya: agree. also surface KV miss ratio trend: if miss ratio spikes, that could explain disk latency in waterfall
Maya L: ok next steps: Jules, wire telemetry + roll aggregation; Samir, measure sampling overhead on staging; Kevin, draft Console mockup; Leo, add fallback policy options; I'll schedule a 30m sync next Tue. thanks everyone :rocket:
Kevin: thanks — I sketched a mock in Figma and linked in the issue (https://figma/s/IR-672) :art:
